note: Receiver cases. Each gives the perigraph attributes of one record and what a conforming receiver does with them: `rejected` (not a record of this version), or `stored` with whether a verdict over this record alone is `admissible` or `refused` (SPEC section 0.5). A rejected case says whether spec/schema/record.schema.json alone rejects it too (`schema`): the ones it accepts are rejected only by recomputing an identity. Run them with tools/conform.py. Comparisons between records are not covered here; see conformance/README.md.

cases.description: A record from a request adapter: instruction held, the rest absent, the model half not_observable.
The same record with a model half a stamper loaded, carrying model and artifact identities.
No model half at all. It does not conform as a sender's record, and a receiver still stores it and does not refuse a verdict for it.
Most parts are not mentioned at all. A record missing any number of parts is stored, never rejected.
A manifest naming a part twice is read as a set.
Empty entries in a manifest are dropped, not read as a part named empty-string.
A vendor extension key is ignored, never grounds for rejection.
Attributes outside the perigraph. prefix belong to the span and are not the record's.
Status collector_failed: stored as a log, and no verdict.
Status aborted: stored as a log, and no verdict.
No identifying part, so no harness identity: stored, no verdict.
The manifest claims tool_schemas and the record reports it not_reachable.

attributes.perigraph.part.decoding.label: temperature
attributes.perigraph.absent.tool_schemas.detail: tools were stripped by an upstream proxy before this collector saw the request

cases.description: The manifest claims readout and the record says nothing about it.
A spec_version this receiver does not implement.
A part outside the closed list.
A sourcing value outside the vocabulary.
An absence reason outside the vocabulary.
A status outside the vocabulary.
A boundary outside the vocabulary.
One part both held and absent.
A pulled_by_us part with no read lag.
A read lag on a part that was in the request.
extraction_failed blames the collector and carries no detail.
not_provided blames the requester and carries a detail.
A harness identity that is not the one derived from the parts carried.
An empty harness identity string on a record with none. An identity is omitted, never empty.
A model identity that is not the one derived from the model parts carried.
A model identity on a record whose model parts are not_observable.
A harness part with sourcing loaded_by_us, which only a model part can have.
A model part with sourcing in_the_request: a request does not carry weights.
A part recorded not_observable that carries a digest.
